dek.text: The state's chip fund is backing a Texas Tech computing cluster in Lubbock with over $19 million. The announcement gives no date for when the cluster will run.

introduction.text: [Texas Tech's college of engineering received another Texas Semiconductor Innovation Fund award worth over {{money:c1}} million](c1). [The university announced it on {{date:c2}}](c2). [The money will help Texas Tech set up a next-generation computing cluster in Lubbock](c3).

[The announcement says the award will help establish the cluster. It gives no install or completion date](c4). A reader of the announcement learns what the money is for and not when the machine will exist.

paragraphs.text: [The university describes a computing cluster as linked high-performance servers that work as one system on large parallel workloads](c5). [The project will combine artificial intelligence with high-fidelity simulation data and lab results](c6). [The stated goal is faster development of new semiconductor devices and materials](c7).

[The university says conventional semiconductor design leans on physics-based modeling that can be computationally intensive](c12). [Planned research includes AI-driven discovery and modeling of materials](c10), [and using AI to guide the epitaxial growth of ultrawide-bandgap semiconductors](c11).

[Roland Faller, dean of the Whitacre College of Engineering, is on the research team](c9). [He says Texas Tech will be among the first universities with access to the newest generation of Nvidia chips to power the cluster](c8). That is the dean's statement about access, and the announcement names no chip count and no delivery date.

[This is not Texas Tech's first award from the fund. Earlier awards paid for a new clean room and for semiconductors meant for harsh environments](c14). [In January the fund awarded Texas Tech {{money:c15}} million toward the clean room](c15). [The university will match that state money for a clean room project of {{money:c16}} million](c16).

[In May a team at the same college received roughly {{money:c17}} million for wide and ultrawide bandgap semiconductor research](c17). The three figures are not alike. January's is stated as a whole figure, May's is approximate and November's is a floor, so no total can be stated honestly.

[The fund's grants are administered by the Texas CHIPS Office in the Office of the Governor](c18). [The Texas CHIPS Act, signed in {{number:c19}}, created the fund](c19). [Texas Tech President Lawrence Schovanec thanked Governor Abbott and state leaders for the investment](c13).
The open question as of the announcement is the schedule. Nothing in the three announcements says when the Lubbock cluster will be installed or when its first research will run.
